original_test_intent: Read BMC time-zone information from Redfish and verify it matches a platform specification.
original_method: Resolve the exact Manager resource, preserve the complete response, extract schema-defined standard and OEM time-zone fields independently and compare them to an approved policy at a recorded UTC instant using explicit DST/offset normalization.
manual_activity: Provide the exact Manager endpoint, target timezone policy and authoritative mapping between DateTimeLocalOffset, any named/OEM zone and daylight-saving behavior.
required_inputs: Expected IANA zone or fixed-offset policy
Expected DateTimeLocalOffset at the observation instant
DST transition rules and applicable date
safety_requirements: No hardcoded credentials or TLS bypass
GET only; never PATCH DateTime or offset
Do not infer an IANA zone solely from an offset
Evaluate standard and OEM fields independently
Do not treat current DST offset as year-round policy
agent_execution_scope: Validate standard and OEM time-field schema
Use secret-backed read-only authentication over verified TLS
Capture status and complete Manager JSON
Extract DateTime, DateTimeLocalOffset and named/OEM zone fields separately
Compute expected offset for the instant when policy permits
Report conflicts without choosing one silently

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The Manager GET is plausible, but the jq comma/pipe expression does not reliably retain both standard and OEM values, the path is assumed, TLS is bypassed and no expected zone or offset exists for comparison.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Discover and securely GET the Manager once, retain complete JSON, extract each standard/OEM time-zone field with an explicit object projection and compare it at a recorded UTC instant to the approved DST-aware policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Time Zone scope and 15/10 timing remain; ManagerId, policy zone, offset, DST state and OEM precedence are not inferred.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a timestamped semantic comparison that distinguishes named-zone policy from the instantaneous numeric offset and retains every authoritative field separately.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces the placeholder and ambiguous filter with endpoint discovery, complete evidence, an external oracle, DST-aware computation and explicit standard/OEM conflict handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Validates reported timezone configuration only; it does not set the zone, alter DateTime, prove NTP synchronization or test behavior across a DST transition.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Many zones share the same offset at a given instant, so offset equality alone cannot prove the intended geographic timezone.

project_override_considerations: If the platform specification defines only a fixed numeric offset, do not manufacture an IANA zone requirement. If a named zone is required but Redfish exposes only an offset, report the coverage limitation rather than guessing from geography.
expected_evidence: UTC observation timestamp and applicable DST state
HTTP status and complete response hash
Raw DateTimeLocalOffset and named/OEM zone fields
Explicit standard/OEM conflict or coverage limitation
No time mutation and preserved logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Script and Criteria consistently request a read-only Time Zone versus specification check. The placeholder and missing oracle make it incomplete, but no competing operation is stated.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The endpoint/schema, expected timezone policy and DST normalization are identifiable package inputs, so the case is REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Reclassifies a placeholder and faulty field projection into a timestamped, DST-aware comparison that cannot confuse a transient UTC offset with a named timezone policy.
independent_technical_reasoning: `DateTimeLocalOffset` is an instantaneous numeric relationship to UTC, not a unique zone name. Multiple IANA zones share offsets, and daylight-saving rules can change the expected offset by date. A reliable comparison must record the UTC observation time, know whether the specification requires a named zone or fixed offset, and evaluate standard and OEM fields without jq precedence loss. The test remains read-only; changing the clock would affect logs, certificates and scheduled operations and is outside this row.
